title: JavaScript Quiz
description: Test your knowledge of JavaScript fundamentals.

questions.question: What does `typeof null` return in JavaScript?
questions.explanation: `typeof null` returns "object". This is a long-standing quirk of the language.

questions.question: Which keyword declares a block-scoped variable that cannot be reassigned?
questions.explanation: `const` creates a block-scoped binding that cannot be reassigned.

questions.question: What does `"3" + 2` evaluate to?
questions.explanation: With the + operator, if one operand is a string the other is converted to a string, so the result is "32".

questions.question: What does `Array.prototype.map()` return?
questions.explanation: `map()` returns a new array with the results of calling the callback on every element.

questions.question: What is the difference between `==` and `===`?
options: `===` compares only values, `==` compares value and type
`==` allows type coercion, `===` compares value and type strictly
questions.explanation: `==` performs type coercion before comparing, while `===` requires both value and type to match.

questions.question: Which method adds an element to the end of an array?
questions.explanation: `push()` appends one or more elements to the end of an array.

questions.question: What is a closure in JavaScript?
options: A function that has no parameters
A function bundled with access to its surrounding lexical scope
A way to close a browser window
A method that ends a loop
questions.explanation: A closure lets a function remember and access variables from the scope where it was created.

questions.question: What does the `await` keyword do?
options: Blocks the entire program until a promise resolves
Pauses the async function until the promise settles
questions.explanation: `await` pauses execution of the async function until the promise settles, without blocking the main thread.

questions.question: What does `NaN === NaN` evaluate to?
questions.explanation: NaN is the only value in JavaScript that is not equal to itself. Use `Number.isNaN()` to check for it.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a primitive type in JavaScript?
questions.explanation: Arrays are objects. The primitive types are string, number, bigint, boolean, undefined, null and symbol.
